t: Suleiman asked Sinan for a mosque of his own after the Şehzade Mosque, intending one that would surpass all those built by his predecessors and represent the pre-eminence of the Ottoman Empire.

Its prayer hall follows the dome-and-semi-dome plan of the Hagia Sophia and the Bayezid II Mosque, but Sinan hid most of the buttresses in the walls so that the outside rises towards the central dome.
The mosque stood at the centre of a külliye of madrasas, a hospital, a public kitchen and other buildings, and behind its qibla wall lie the octagonal mausoleums of Suleiman and Hürrem Sultan.
dyk: The four minarets have ten balconies in all, which is said to reflect that Suleiman I was the 10th Ottoman sultan.
ev: The foundation date given by the Arabic inscription above the entrance to the prayer hall, although planning began earlier
The inauguration date given by the same inscription, though parts of the complex were finished later
Suleiman died, and his son Selim II ordered the building of his mausoleum, completed between 1566 and 1568
A great fire damaged the mosque, and Sultan Mehmed IV restored it
Part of the dome collapsed in an earthquake, and the repairs damaged what remained of Sinan's decoration
Extensive repairs were made to the interior, the minarets, the outer courtyard and the tombs
A restoration of the prayer hall began, removing 19th-century wall decoration and reviving earlier designs beneath it
The most comprehensive modern restoration began, preserving original mortar, plaster and decoration in place

f.made: Commissioned by Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent (r. 1520–1566) and designed by the imperial architect Mimar Sinan; the foundation inscription was composed by Ebussuud Efendi and calligraphed by Hasan Çelebi
f.form: A domed imperial mosque with a prayer hall of 58.5 by 57.5 metres under a central dome 53 metres high and 26.5 metres across, a courtyard of around 47 by 57 metres and four minarets, at the centre of a külliye (religious and charitable complex)
f.where: On the Third Hill of Istanbul, Turkey, above the Golden Horn; part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site "Historic Areas of Istanbul"
f.known: the largest Ottoman-era mosque in Istanbul; the central dome modelled on the Hagia Sophia; four minarets with ten balconies; restrained decoration and thuluth calligraphy; the mausoleums of Suleiman and Hürrem Sultan; the surrounding complex of madrasas, kitchen and hospital
